description: RECONSTRUCTION, not a transcription. The source declares fourteen status values, four named subsets of them, and which status each queue binds; it declares no transition table, and the function that changes a status checks membership only. Every transition below carries the evidence it was assembled from. Read at v3.9.0.

requested.description: Written by whoever asked — the API, the rules engine, or the workflow engine. The scheduler's queue binds this key.

SCHEDULED.description: The scheduler admitted the item past its policies.

DELAYED.description: A policy held the item back; the scheduler writes this without publishing it.

CANCELING.description: requested is a member of the cancelable set.

delayed.description: Held by a concurrency or throttling policy. The scheduler revisits it.

SCHEDULED.description: The scheduler re-examines delayed items alongside requested ones.

CANCELING.description: delayed is a member of the cancelable set.

scheduled.description: Admitted. The runners' work queue binds this key, and whichever runner is free takes it.

RUNNING.description: The runner stamps its own process information and starts the action.

CANCELING.description: A cancel may arrive between admission and start.

running.description: A runner process is executing the action.

SUCCEEDED.description: Terminal status returned by the runner. Member of the completed set.

FAILED.description: Returned by the runner, or written by the worker when the dispatch raised.

TIMEOUT.description: Member of the completed and failed sets; the runner enforces its own timeout parameter.

ABANDONED.description: Written when a worker shuts down with the item still incomplete.

PENDING.description: The inquirer runner returns this instead of a terminal status when it asks a human a question.

PAUSING.description: Only runners that support pausing act on it.

CANCELING.description: running is a member of the cancelable set.

pending.description: Waiting for a human to answer an inquiry. Not a member of the completed set, so nothing downstream treats it as finished.

SUCCEEDED.description: Answering the inquiry writes succeeded and asks for the parent workflow to resume.

CANCELING.description: An unanswered inquiry can be cancelled like anything else.

pausing.description: Pause requested. The runners' pause queue binds this key.

PAUSED.description: The runner reports the work is held.

CANCELING.description: pausing is a member of the cancelable set.

paused.description: Held. Member of the runnable set, which is what lets it be picked up again.

RESUMING.description: Resume requested; the runners' resume queue binds this key.

CANCELING.description: paused is a member of the cancelable set.

RUNNING.description: The runner picks the work up again.

CANCELING.description: resuming is a member of the cancelable set.

canceling.description: Cancel requested. The runners' cancel queue binds this key, and the runner that takes it need not be the one holding the work.

CANCELED.description: The runner reports the work stopped. Member of the completed set.

ABANDONED.description: A worker shutting down mid-cancel abandons the item instead.
